why: Kedar here means the nomadic tribe whose dark tents the woman compares herself to, not the patriarch Kedar as a person. Pharaoh's chariots in 1:9 are a comparison to Egyptian war horses, not any particular pharaoh.
'David's tower' in 4:4 names a tower, probably a fortification known to the poet's hearers; the verse does not speak of David the man, and which tower is meant is not known.
Bible Atlas links the Carmel in the Judean hills near Maon, but 7:5 compares her head to Mount Carmel, the mountain ridge by the northern coast, so the link now points there.
Bible Atlas draws Baal-hamon on the same point as Senir, in the Hermon range, but nobody knows where Solomon's vineyard at Baal-hamon was, so no dot is drawn.
